chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqqah, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Ibrahim ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
'The matter of God, all of it, is wondrous — except that He has argued against you with what He has already made known to you of Himself.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: The affair/matter of God — encompassing all of God's decrees, actions, and attributes
key_terms.احْتَجَّ: He argued/established the proof (hujja) — God's divine argument against humanity
key_terms.عَجِيبٌ: Wondrous, strange, extraordinary — beyond ordinary human comprehension
key_terms.عَرَّفَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: What He has made known to you of Himself — referring to innate knowledge (fitra) of God

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about God's argument against humanity in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms a paradox at the heart of theology: while all of God's affairs are beyond ordinary comprehension, God has been just and gracious in establishing the proof of His existence through the very knowledge of Himself He has implanted within human nature (fitra). This hadith teaches that divine self-disclosure is the basis of religious obligation — humans cannot claim ignorance of God because God has made Himself known to them through innate recognition. It appears in the chapter on the lowest level of recognition (ma'rifa), suggesting that even the minimum required knowledge of God is already present in every human being.
word_analysis: made known to you/introduced to you
